function: CSI feedback: UE compresses downlink CSI with analog deep joint source-channel coding, BS reconstructs it, adapting features and bandwidth to the channel scenario label (p. 3, p. 7).
system: FDD MIMO-OFDM, BS with 32 antennas, single-antenna UE, 128 subcarriers, uplink 5.4 GHz and downlink 5.6 GHz, no RIS (p. 10).
method: Swin-Transformer DJSCC encoder-decoder with scenario-label attention and learned bandwidth masker; supervised end-to-end MSE training on mixed scenarios, two-stage initialization (p. 3-8, p. 13).
data_channel: 3GPP TR 38.901 CDL-A to CDL-E generated with Sionna; per scenario 50,000 training, 10,000 validation, 10,000 test samples (p. 9-10).
test_conditions: Train on mixed CDL-A..E, feedback SNR uniform in [-10,10] dB; test on same five scenarios, SNR -10 to 10 dB; label-mismatch test at 10 dB (p. 10-13).
baselines: Learned: SJSCC (Swin ADJSCC, single-scenario and mixed training), MT-SJSCC, MT-CsiNet (SSCC with 2-bit quantizer, QAM, channel coding), AnalogDeepCMC (complexity only); no codebook or compressed-sensing baseline (p. 10-15).
metrics: NMSE of CSI reconstruction versus SNR; bandwidth compression ratio (BCR) and bandwidth savings; FLOPs and parameter count (p. 10, p. 13, p. 15).
complexity: Table 2: JSBANet 0.1875 GFLOPs and 4.38 M parameters; SJSCC 0.1599 GFLOPs, 1.86 M per scenario; AnalogDeepCMC 0.3322 GFLOPs, 10.80 M (p. 15).
openness: none; data generated with the open-source Sionna library, no link to code or dataset (p. 9).
q1_support: p. 9: "We adopt the CDL channel models specified in 3GPP TR 38.901" and generate the data with Sionna.
q2_support: p. 10: "All trained models are evaluated on the mixed-scenario dataset"; SA-SDJSCC is trained on mixed CDL-A..E, so every tested scenario was seen in training. Unseen-scenario tests apply only to single-scenario SJSCC baselines.
q3_support: p. 12: "MT-CsiNet (SSCC Baseline): This model adopts the traditional SSCC architecture"; its source encoder is a learned multi-task CsiNet. Learned baselines SJSCC and MT-SJSCC are compared, but no non-learned method (codebook, compressed sensing) is.
q4_support: p. 15: "Table 2 summarizes the floating-point operations (FLOPs) and the number of trainable parameters"; JSBANet 0.1875 G FLOPs, 4.38 M parameters.
q5_support: p. 9: "use the open-source Python library Sionna to generate the CSI datasets"; data are simulated, no link to code or dataset; p. 10 puts measurement data outside the scope of the study.
notes: Include, area 2 (CSI feedback; BS 32 antennas, so the single-antenna exclusion does not apply). q2 is 0: no unseen scenario, band, or antenna count for the proposed model; Fig. 13 (p. 12) mislabels the scenario label on the seen scenarios, comparable to a robustness sweep. q3 is 0 and borderline: the SSCC baseline is described as traditional, but its source coder is learned, and no purely non-learned comparator is reported. Ideal uplink and downlink CSI are assumed (p. 3).
